JOR.summary: A compact country that packs in a rock-cut ancient city, a red-sand desert and the lowest point on Earth. Easy to drive yourself and manageable in a week.
JOR.bestTimeNote: Spring and autumn are warm and dry. Summer is very hot in the desert and at the Dead Sea; winter nights are cold in Petra and Wadi Rum.

places.name: Amman
places.blurb: The capital: a Roman theatre, the hilltop Citadel and the best food in the country.

places.name: Petra
places.blurb: The Nabataean city carved into rose-coloured cliffs. Give it two days to reach the Monastery.

places.name: Wadi Rum
places.blurb: Sandstone mountains and red dunes. Stay a night in a desert camp.

places.name: Dead Sea
places.blurb: Float in the salt water at the lowest point on Earth, then do nothing for a day.

tips: Hiring a car is the simplest way to link Amman, Petra, Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea.
Start Petra at opening time to see the Treasury before the crowds.

VNM.summary: A long, thin country best travelled north to south or the reverse: limestone bays, old trading towns, big energetic cities and some of the best street food in Asia.
VNM.bestTimeNote: The weather differs a lot between north, centre and south, so no month is perfect everywhere. Spring and late autumn are the safest all-round choices.

places.name: Hanoi
places.blurb: The Old Quarter, lakes and street food. A good place to start or finish.

places.name: Ha Long Bay
places.blurb: Thousands of limestone islands, usually seen on an overnight boat.

places.name: Ninh Binh
places.blurb: Karst peaks rising out of rice paddies, explored by rowing boat and bicycle.

places.name: Hue
places.blurb: The old imperial capital, with its citadel and royal tombs.

places.name: Hoi An
places.blurb: A lantern-lit old trading port known for tailors, food and nearby beaches.

places.name: Ho Chi Minh City
places.blurb: The fast-moving southern hub, and the gateway to the Mekong Delta.

places.name: Ha Giang
places.blurb: The far-northern mountains, best seen on a three or four day motorbike loop over high passes.

places.name: Sa Pa
places.blurb: A hill town above terraced rice valleys, for trekking between minority villages.

places.name: Cat Ba
places.blurb: A rugged island on the edge of Ha Long Bay, and the base for quieter Lan Ha Bay.

places.name: Da Nang
places.blurb: A modern beach city with the main airport of central Vietnam, between Hue and Hoi An.

places.name: Da Lat
places.blurb: A cool hill town of pine forest, waterfalls, flower farms and coffee.

places.name: Phu Quoc
places.blurb: A large island in the far south, for white-sand beaches and a few lazy days at the end of a trip.

places.name: Nha Trang
places.blurb: A busy beach resort city on a long bay, with islands and diving offshore.

places.name: Mui Ne
places.blurb: A beach strip known for kitesurfing, with red and white sand dunes just inland.

tips: Internal flights are cheap and save a lot of time on a country this long.
Check entry requirements before you book.

ITA.summary: Art cities, hill towns, coast and mountains, joined up by fast trains. Works as a city break, a food trip or a full fortnight.
ITA.bestTimeNote: Late spring and early autumn are warm without the peak crowds. July and August are hot and busy, especially in the cities.

places.name: Rome
places.blurb: The Colosseum, the Forum, the Vatican, and long lunches in between.

places.name: Florence
places.blurb: Renaissance art and architecture, and the base for Tuscany.

places.name: Venice
places.blurb: Canals and back alleys. Stay overnight to see it after the day trippers leave.

places.name: Cinque Terre
places.blurb: Five cliffside villages linked by coastal paths and a local train.

places.name: Amalfi Coast
places.blurb: Steep villages above the sea south of Naples, with Pompeii close by.

places.name: Dolomites
places.blurb: Jagged peaks for summer hiking and winter skiing.

places.name: Milan
places.blurb: The Duomo, Leonardo's Last Supper and the country's fashion and design capital.

places.name: Naples
places.blurb: Loud, crowded and full of life: the home of pizza, with Pompeii and Vesuvius next door.

places.name: Bologna
places.blurb: Miles of arcaded streets, medieval towers and some of the best food in Italy.

places.name: Pisa
places.blurb: The Leaning Tower and its cathedral square, an easy stop between Florence and the coast.

places.name: Stelvio Pass
places.blurb: Forty-eight hairpin bends up to one of the highest road passes in the Alps. Open in summer only.

places.name: Colosseum
places.blurb: Rome's great amphitheatre, with the Forum and the Palatine Hill beside it on the same ticket.

places.name: Lake Como
places.blurb: A long, deep lake under steep mountains, with villas, gardens and ferries between the villages.

places.name: Lake Garda
places.blurb: Italy's largest lake: lemon groves and castles in the south, cliffs and windsurfing in the north.

tips: Trains between the main cities are fast and frequent; you only need a car for the countryside.
Book the big museums and sights ahead in high season.

IND.summary: Vast and varied. Most first trips pick one region: the forts and palaces of the north, or the slower, greener south.
IND.bestTimeNote: The cooler dry season is the comfortable time for most of the country. April to June is very hot, and the monsoon follows.

places.name: Delhi
places.blurb: Mughal monuments, markets, and the usual way in to the north.

places.name: Agra
places.blurb: The Taj Mahal, best at sunrise, and Agra Fort.

places.name: Jaipur
places.blurb: The Pink City: Amber Fort, palaces and bazaars.

places.name: Varanasi
places.blurb: One of the world's oldest living cities, on the banks of the Ganges.

places.name: Goa
places.blurb: Beaches and Portuguese-era towns on the west coast.

places.name: Kerala backwaters
places.blurb: Palm-lined canals and lagoons, travelled by houseboat.

places.name: Udaipur
places.blurb: A city of lakes and white palaces in the hills of southern Rajasthan.

places.name: Mumbai
places.blurb: India's biggest city: colonial-era landmarks, Bollywood, street food and the sea all along one side.

places.name: Ranthambore National Park
places.blurb: The best-known place in India to see wild tigers, on jeep safaris around a ruined hilltop fort.

places.name: Ahmedabad
places.blurb: Gandhi's ashram, carved stepwells and a walled old city of narrow lanes.

tips: Distances are large: choose one region rather than trying to cover the country.
Check entry requirements before you book.

NZL.summary: Two islands made for a road trip: geothermal valleys and beaches in the north, mountains, fjords and glaciers in the south.
NZL.bestTimeNote: Summer and early autumn give long days and settled weather. June to September is ski season in the South Island.

places.name: Auckland
places.blurb: The main arrival city, built around harbours and volcanic cones.

places.name: Rotorua
places.blurb: Geysers, hot pools and Maori culture.

places.name: Wellington
places.blurb: The small, walkable capital, and the ferry port for the South Island.

places.name: Abel Tasman
places.blurb: Golden beaches and a coastal track, on foot or by kayak.

places.name: Queenstown
places.blurb: A lakeside adventure town ringed by mountains.

places.name: Milford Sound
places.blurb: A fjord of sheer cliffs and waterfalls, reached by one of the great drives.

places.name: Mount Cook
places.blurb: Aoraki, the country's highest peak, with glacier lakes and the Hooker Valley walk from the village at its foot.

places.name: Wanaka
places.blurb: A lakeside town quieter than Queenstown, with the Roys Peak hike and Mount Aspiring National Park behind.

places.name: Franz Josef
places.blurb: A West Coast village below a glacier that drops almost to the rainforest, seen on foot or by helicopter.

places.name: Lake Tekapo
places.blurb: A milky-turquoise lake with a tiny stone church on the shore, under some of the darkest night skies in the world.

places.name: Kaikoura
places.blurb: A coastal town between mountains and deep ocean, for whale watching, dolphins, seals and crayfish.

places.name: Christchurch
places.blurb: The South Island's main city, rebuilt after its earthquakes, with gardens, a river through the centre and the main airport.

places.name: Taupo
places.blurb: A town on the country's largest lake, with Huka Falls, hot pools and the Tongariro Alpine Crossing nearby.

places.name: Te Anau
places.blurb: A lakeside town on the edge of Fiordland, and the base for Milford Sound and the Kepler and Milford tracks.

places.name: Waiheke
places.blurb: An island of vineyards, olive groves and beaches, forty minutes by ferry from Auckland.

places.name: Arthur's Pass
places.blurb: A mountain village on the road and railway across the Southern Alps, with short walks to waterfalls and cheeky kea.

places.name: Hokitika
places.blurb: A West Coast beach town known for greenstone carving, with the turquoise Hokitika Gorge inland.

places.name: Fairlie
places.blurb: A small farming town at the gateway to the Mackenzie Country, famous for its pies.

tips: Driving times are longer than the map suggests; plan fewer stops with more nights.
Hire cars and campervans sell out in summer, so book early.

USA.summary: Too big for one trip. Pick a region: the cities of the east, the national parks of the west, or a road trip through the south.
USA.bestTimeNote: It depends heavily on the region. Late spring and early autumn suit most cities and parks; desert parks are very hot in summer.

places.name: New York
places.blurb: Museums, food, neighbourhoods and skyline. Four nights barely covers it.

places.name: New Orleans
places.blurb: Live music, Creole food and the French Quarter.

places.name: Grand Canyon
places.blurb: Stay near the rim for sunrise and sunset.

places.name: Yellowstone
places.blurb: Geysers, hot springs, bison and bears in the first national park.

places.name: Yosemite
places.blurb: Granite cliffs, waterfalls and giant sequoias.

places.name: San Francisco
places.blurb: Hills, the bay and the Golden Gate, and the start of the coast road south.

places.name: Los Angeles
places.blurb: Hollywood, Venice Beach and Santa Monica, museums and food from everywhere, spread across a vast sunny sprawl.

places.name: Las Vegas
places.blurb: Casinos, shows and neon in the Nevada desert, and a handy base for the Grand Canyon and Death Valley.

places.name: Chicago
places.blurb: Skyscraper architecture on Lake Michigan, blues clubs, big museums and deep-dish pizza.

places.name: Hawaii
places.blurb: Volcanic islands in the middle of the Pacific, with surf beaches, lava fields and green cliffs. Honolulu is the usual way in.

places.name: Alaska
places.blurb: Glaciers, bears, whales and the highest mountain in North America, on a scale that needs at least a week. Anchorage is the usual start.

places.name: Death Valley National Park
places.blurb: The hottest, driest and lowest place in North America: salt flats, sand dunes and painted badlands.

places.name: Mount Rushmore
places.blurb: Four presidents carved into a granite mountain in the Black Hills of South Dakota.

places.name: Philadelphia
places.blurb: Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell, where the United States began, plus great museums and cheesesteaks.

places.name: Dallas
places.blurb: A big, modern Texan city, with the museum on the Kennedy assassination and a large arts district.

places.name: Fort Worth
places.blurb: The cowboy side of Texas: the old Stockyards, a daily cattle drive, rodeos and honky-tonks.

places.name: Albuquerque
places.blurb: An adobe old town on Route 66, a cable car up the Sandia mountains and a hot-air balloon fiesta each October.

places.name: El Paso
places.blurb: A desert city in far west Texas on the Rio Grande, facing Mexico, with old Spanish missions nearby.

places.name: Indianapolis
places.blurb: The home of the Indianapolis 500, with the Speedway and its museum open all year.

places.name: Rachel
places.blurb: A speck of a town on Nevada's Extraterrestrial Highway, the closest place to Area 51, with an alien-themed diner and motel.

tips: Outside the big cities you will need a car.
Check entry requirements before you book.

FRA.summary: Paris is the obvious start, but the country rewards going further: wine regions, the Alps and the Mediterranean coast are all a fast train away.
FRA.bestTimeNote: Late spring and early autumn are the pleasant months. August is busy on the coast and quiet in Paris; the Alps have a winter ski season.

places.name: Paris
places.blurb: Museums, cafes and long walks along the Seine.

places.name: Lille
places.blurb: Flemish squares, a big art museum and good beer, an hour north of Paris by train.

places.name: Val Thorens
places.blurb: The highest ski resort in Europe, at the top of the huge Three Valleys area, with snow from November to May.

tips: High-speed trains make most of the country reachable from Paris in a few hours.

GB-ENG.summary: From London's museums and theatres to northern cities, Lake District fells and the beaches of the south-west.

places.name: London
places.blurb: Museums, theatre, markets and royal parks. Four nights covers the main sights without rushing.

places.name: Lake District
places.blurb: Lakes, fells and stone villages: England's best walking country.

places.name: Cornwall
places.blurb: Surf beaches, fishing harbours and the coast path, at the far south-west tip.

places.name: Devon
places.blurb: Two coasts, Dartmoor in between, and cream teas everywhere.

places.name: Manchester
places.blurb: Music, football and industrial history in the big city of the north-west.

places.name: Liverpool
places.blurb: The Beatles, the waterfront docks and two football clubs.

places.name: Seven Sisters
places.blurb: A line of white chalk cliffs on the Sussex coast, with a clifftop walk along the top.

places.name: Bath
places.blurb: Roman baths and honey-coloured Georgian crescents, in a city small enough to walk.

places.name: Oxford
places.blurb: Old colleges, quiet quads and riverside pubs, an hour from London.

places.name: Brighton
places.blurb: A pebble beach, a pier and the narrow shopping streets of the Lanes, in the liveliest town on the south coast.

places.name: Peak District
places.blurb: Gritstone edges, limestone dales and stone villages, between Manchester and Sheffield.

places.name: Norfolk
places.blurb: Wide sandy beaches, seals and salt marsh on the north coast, with the Broads inland.

places.name: Mablethorpe
places.blurb: A traditional seaside town on the Lincolnshire coast, with a long sandy beach and dunes.

MYS.summary: Skyscrapers and street food in the capital, with rainforest, islands and Borneo beyond.

places.name: Kuala Lumpur
places.blurb: The Petronas Towers, the Batu Caves and some of Asia's best street food.

places.name: Penang
places.blurb: The old streets of George Town, with street art, clan houses and the best hawker food in Malaysia.

places.name: Langkawi
places.blurb: A duty-free island of beaches, jungle and a cable car up to a bridge in the sky.

CHN.summary: Imperial palaces, the Great Wall and enormous modern cities.

places.name: Beijing
places.blurb: The Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven and day trips out to the Great Wall.

places.name: Forbidden City
places.blurb: The emperors' palace in the middle of Beijing, with almost a thousand buildings behind red walls. Book ahead.

places.name: Mutianyu Great Wall
places.blurb: A restored stretch of the Great Wall over wooded hills, quieter than Badaling and a day trip from Beijing.

places.name: Shanghai
places.blurb: The Bund's old waterfront facing the towers of Pudong, in China's biggest and most modern city.

places.name: Xi'an
places.blurb: The old capital at the start of the Silk Road, with complete city walls and a busy Muslim Quarter.

places.name: Terracotta Warriors
places.blurb: Thousands of life-size clay soldiers guarding the first emperor's tomb, just outside Xi'an.

places.name: Chengdu
places.blurb: The home of giant pandas, teahouses and fiery Sichuan food.

places.name: Zhangjiajie
places.blurb: A forest of sandstone pillars rising out of the mist, with glass bridges and cliff walkways.

places.name: Yangshuo
places.blurb: Limestone peaks along the Li River, explored by bamboo raft and bicycle.

places.name: Lhasa
places.blurb: The Potala Palace and the Jokhang Temple, high on the Tibetan plateau. Foreign visitors need a permit and an organised tour.

places.name: Jiuzhaigou Valley
places.blurb: Turquoise lakes, waterfalls and forest in a high valley in northern Sichuan.

places.name: Suzhou
places.blurb: Classical gardens and canals, half an hour from Shanghai by fast train.

places.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
places.blurb: A seated Buddha 71 metres tall, carved into a river cliff. A day trip from Chengdu.

places.name: Chongqing
places.blurb: A vast city stacked on hills above the Yangtze, famous for its hotpot and its night-time skyline.

places.name: Harbin
places.blurb: A far-northern city with Russian architecture and a huge ice and snow festival in January and February.

places.name: Sanya
places.blurb: China's tropical beach resort, at the southern tip of Hainan island.

places.name: Hainan
places.blurb: A tropical island off the south coast, with beaches, rainforest and volcanic hot springs. Haikou is the capital.

places.name: Dandong
places.blurb: A border city on the Yalu River, looking straight across to North Korea.

places.name: Urumqi
places.blurb: The capital of Xinjiang in the far west, with bazaars and the mountain lake of Tianchi nearby.

places.name: Shijiazhuang Table Tennis Centre
places.blurb: The national table tennis training base at Zhengding, just outside Shijiazhuang, where China's champions train.

JPN.summary: Neon cities, quiet temples and exceptional food, joined up by very fast trains.

places.name: Tokyo
places.blurb: A vast city of distinct neighbourhoods, from Shibuya's crossing to Asakusa's temples.

places.name: Kyoto
places.blurb: The old imperial capital: hundreds of temples, the gates of Fushimi Inari and the geisha district of Gion.

places.name: Osaka
places.blurb: Japan's kitchen: street food and neon in Dotonbori, a castle and an easy-going feel.

places.name: Mount Fuji
places.blurb: Japan's highest and most famous mountain, seen from the Five Lakes or Hakone and climbed in July and August.

places.name: Hiroshima
places.blurb: The Peace Memorial Park and museum, and the floating shrine gate of Miyajima a short ferry away.

places.name: Nara
places.blurb: A giant bronze Buddha in a vast wooden hall, and a park full of tame deer. An easy day from Kyoto or Osaka.

places.name: Hokkaido
places.blurb: The northern island: powder snow in winter, flower fields and national parks in summer, with Sapporo as the base.

places.name: Okinawa
places.blurb: Subtropical islands far to the south, with beaches, coral reefs and a culture of their own.

places.name: Nagano
places.blurb: A mountain city with a great temple, snow monkeys bathing in hot springs nearby and the ski slopes of the Japan Alps.

places.name: Fukuoka
places.blurb: The main city of Kyushu, known for ramen and its evening food stalls along the river.

HUN.summary: A grand capital on the Danube, known for its thermal baths.

places.name: Budapest
places.blurb: Thermal baths, the castle hill and ruin bars, split in two by the Danube.

CZE.summary: A fairy-tale capital, and castles and beer towns beyond it.

places.name: Prague
places.blurb: The castle, Charles Bridge and an old town of spires and cobbled lanes.

PRT.summary: Tiled cities, Atlantic beaches and good food at gentle prices.

places.name: Lisbon
places.blurb: Hills, trams and tiled streets above the Tagus, with beaches a short train ride away.

places.name: Porto
places.blurb: Steep streets down to the Douro, port cellars across the river and the valley's vineyards beyond.

places.name: Coimbra
places.blurb: A hilltop university town between Lisbon and Porto, with a great baroque library.

places.name: Reine
places.blurb: A fishing village in the Lofoten Islands, ringed by sharp peaks rising out of the sea.

places.name: Bergen
places.blurb: Painted wooden wharves, a fish market and seven hills, and the gateway to the western fjords.

places.name: Oslo
places.blurb: A waterfront capital with an opera house you can walk on, Viking ships and forest at the end of the metro.

places.name: Alesund
places.blurb: An art nouveau town spread over islands, with the Geirangerfjord within reach.

places.name: Svolvaer
places.blurb: The main town of the Lofoten Islands, with ferries, boat trips to Trollfjord and the peaks behind.

places.name: Henningsvaer
places.blurb: A Lofoten fishing village spread over small islands, with galleries, cafes and a famous football pitch.

places.name: Bodo
places.blurb: A small city north of the Arctic Circle, and where the ferry leaves for the Lofoten Islands.

places.name: Å
places.blurb: The last village on the Lofoten road, with red fishing cabins and a stockfish museum.

places.name: Leknes
places.blurb: The practical centre of Lofoten, with an airport and the beaches of Haukland and Uttakleiv nearby.

places.name: Mortsund
places.blurb: A quiet Lofoten fishing hamlet of cabins on the water, a short drive from Leknes.

GB-SCT.summary: A handsome capital, then lochs, glens and mountains all the way north.

places.name: Edinburgh
places.blurb: The castle, the Royal Mile and Arthur's Seat, in a city built for walking.

places.name: Loch Lomond
places.blurb: Britain's largest lake, with wooded islands and the first of the Highland hills.

places.name: Cairngorms
places.blurb: High mountain plateau, pine forest and wildlife, with Aviemore as the base.

places.name: Inverness
places.blurb: The small capital of the Highlands, on the doorstep of Loch Ness.

places.name: Isle of Skye
places.blurb: The Cuillin mountains, the Old Man of Storr and sea cliffs, reached by a bridge from the mainland.

places.name: Ben Nevis
places.blurb: Britain's highest mountain, a full day's climb from Fort William at its foot.

GB-WLS.summary: Mountains, castles and a long, wild coast.

places.name: Snowdonia
places.blurb: Wales's highest peaks, slate villages and mountain lakes, around Snowdon itself.

places.name: Anglesey
places.blurb: A low green island off the north coast, with beaches, a coast path and Beaumaris Castle.

IRL.summary: A sociable capital, then green countryside and a wild Atlantic coast.

places.name: Dublin
places.blurb: Georgian squares, Trinity College and the Book of Kells, and a pub on every corner.

GB-NIR.summary: A city with a shipbuilding past, and a coast road north to basalt cliffs.

places.name: Belfast
places.blurb: The Titanic's shipyard, Victorian markets and the murals of a city that has remade itself.

places.name: Giant's Causeway
places.blurb: Forty thousand basalt columns stepping into the sea on the north Antrim coast.

BEL.summary: Grand squares, medieval canals, and beer, chocolate and chips done properly.

places.name: Brussels
places.blurb: The Grand Place, art nouveau streets and the country's best bars and chip stands.

places.name: Bruges
places.blurb: Canals, cobbled lanes and a belfry, in a medieval town that has barely changed.

NLD.summary: Canals, bicycles and great museums, in a flat country that is easy to get around.

places.name: Amsterdam
places.blurb: Canal houses, the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh, best seen on foot or by bike.

DEU.summary: Big cities with plenty of history, and the Alps along the southern edge.

places.name: Berlin
places.blurb: The Wall, Museum Island and the Brandenburg Gate, in a capital still reinventing itself.

places.name: Munich
places.blurb: Beer halls, grand squares and the English Garden, with the Alps an hour south.

places.name: Hamburg
places.blurb: A huge working port, brick warehouses on the water and the Elbphilharmonie concert hall.

LUX.summary: A tiny country around a fortress capital, set among wooded valleys.

places.name: Luxembourg
places.blurb: An old fortress city on cliffs above two river gorges, small enough to see on foot.

LIE.summary: One of the world's smallest countries, squeezed between the Rhine and the Alps.

places.name: Vaduz
places.blurb: The tiny capital, below the prince's castle, with mountains straight up behind it.

CHE.summary: Lakes, mountains and tidy cities, joined up by trains that run to the minute.

places.name: Zurich
places.blurb: A lakeside old town with good museums, and the easiest place to arrive.

places.name: Kandersteg
places.blurb: A mountain village in the Bernese Oberland, with the blue Oeschinen Lake a short walk above it.

places.name: Lugano
places.blurb: Italian-speaking Switzerland: a palm-lined lake, piazzas and mountains behind.

MCO.summary: A tiny, wealthy city-state on the Riviera, seen in a day.

places.name: Monaco
places.blurb: The casino, the harbour full of yachts and the old town on its rock, all within walking distance.

AND.summary: A small mountain country in the Pyrenees, for skiing in winter and walking in summer.

places.name: Arinsal
places.blurb: A ski village at the head of a valley, with lifts into the Vallnord slopes and summer trails above.

ESP.summary: Late nights, great food and very different regions, from Catalonia to Andalusia.

places.name: Barcelona
places.blurb: Gaudí's buildings, the Gothic Quarter and a city beach, with food worth staying up late for.

places.name: Seville
places.blurb: The Alcázar palace, a vast cathedral and orange-tree squares, in the heart of Andalusia.

places.name: Valencia
places.blurb: The home of paella, with an old centre, a futuristic arts quarter and a long beach.

ES-MLL.summary: The largest of the Balearic Islands: a handsome capital, mountains and coves.

places.name: Palma
places.blurb: A huge Gothic cathedral on the seafront and an old town of lanes and courtyards behind it.

GIB.summary: A British territory on a limestone rock at the mouth of the Mediterranean.

places.name: Gibraltar
places.blurb: The Rock: a cable car to the top, Barbary macaques and views across the strait to Africa.

SMR.summary: A tiny hilltop republic surrounded by Italy.

places.name: San Marino
places.blurb: Three towers along a ridge and a walled old town, with views to the Adriatic.

VAT.summary: The world's smallest state, inside Rome.

places.name: Vatican City
places.blurb: St Peter's Basilica, the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel. Book ahead and go early.

places.name: Innsbruck
places.blurb: A painted old town with mountains at the end of every street, and a cable car straight up from the centre.

places.name: Vienna
places.blurb: Imperial palaces, grand coffee houses and a concert or opera most nights of the year.

places.name: Salzburg
places.blurb: Mozart's birthplace: a baroque old town under a hilltop fortress, with lakes and mountains close by.

SVN.summary: A small green country of lakes, gorges and mountains, around an easy-going capital.

places.name: Ljubljana
places.blurb: A small, leafy capital with a castle on the hill and cafes all along the river.

places.name: Lake Bled
places.blurb: An alpine lake with a church on an island and a castle on the cliff above.

places.name: Vintgar Gorge
places.blurb: A boardwalk through a narrow gorge above a clear green river, a few minutes from Bled.

HRV.summary: A long Adriatic coast of walled towns and islands, with lakes and waterfalls inland.

places.name: Dubrovnik
places.blurb: A walled city on the sea. Walk the ramparts early, before the cruise ships arrive.

places.name: Split
places.blurb: A Roman emperor's palace that became the old town, and the main port for the islands.

places.name: Plitvice Lakes
places.blurb: Sixteen turquoise lakes joined by waterfalls, seen from wooden walkways.

places.name: Hvar
places.blurb: A sunny island with a handsome harbour town, lavender fields and boat trips to quiet coves.

places.name: Zadar
places.blurb: Roman ruins and old churches on a small peninsula, with an organ on the seafront played by the waves.

places.name: Krka National Park
places.blurb: A river of wide waterfalls and pools, an easy day trip from Split or Zadar.

SVK.summary: A small capital on the Danube, with castles and the Tatra mountains beyond.

places.name: Bratislava
places.blurb: A compact old town under a white castle, an hour down the Danube from Vienna.

POL.summary: Old market squares, a rebuilt capital and a hard twentieth-century history.

places.name: Krakow
places.blurb: A huge medieval market square, Wawel Castle and the old Jewish quarter of Kazimierz.

places.name: Auschwitz
places.blurb: The Auschwitz-Birkenau memorial and museum, a sobering day trip from Krakow. Book ahead.

places.name: Warsaw
places.blurb: A capital rebuilt from rubble after the war, with a restored old town and strong museums.

places.name: Wroclaw
places.blurb: A colourful market square, islands and bridges on the Oder, and bronze dwarfs hidden all over town.

places.name: Lodz
places.blurb: A former textile city, with mills turned into museums and shops and one very long main street.

BIH.summary: Ottoman bridges, mountain rivers and old towns, a short drive inland from the Adriatic.

places.name: Mostar
places.blurb: The Old Bridge arching over a green river, with a bazaar of cobbled lanes on both banks.

places.name: Trebinje
places.blurb: A quiet town of plane trees, stone houses and local wine, half an hour from Dubrovnik.

SRB.summary: A lively capital where two big rivers meet, with monasteries and hills to the south.

places.name: Belgrade
places.blurb: A fortress above the meeting of the Sava and the Danube, and a city known for its nightlife.

MNE.summary: A small country of steep mountains dropping to the Adriatic.

places.name: Kotor
places.blurb: A walled old town at the end of a fjord-like bay. Climb the fortress steps for the view.

UNK.summary: Europe's youngest country: Ottoman towns, monasteries and high mountains.

places.name: Prizren
places.blurb: Mosques, churches and a stone bridge along a river, below a hilltop fortress.

places.name: Peja
places.blurb: A market town at the mouth of the Rugova Gorge, and the way into the Accursed Mountains.

ALB.summary: Wild mountains in the north, a warm southern coast and a capital full of colour.

places.name: Tirana
places.blurb: A colourful, fast-changing capital, with Cold War bunkers turned into museums.

places.name: Theth
places.blurb: A remote village in the Albanian Alps, reached by a mountain road and ringed by peaks.

places.name: Ksamil
places.blurb: White sand and small islands in clear water, in the far south beside the ruins of Butrint.

places.name: Kruja Castle
places.blurb: The hilltop stronghold of the national hero Skanderbeg, above an old bazaar street.

places.name: Shiroka
places.blurb: A fishing village on the shore of Lake Shkodra, known for its lakeside fish restaurants.

MKD.summary: A lake town of old churches, a capital of statues and a canyon on its doorstep.

places.name: Lake Ohrid
places.blurb: One of Europe's oldest and deepest lakes, with an old town of churches on its shore.

places.name: Skopje
places.blurb: An Ottoman bazaar on one bank and a centre crowded with new statues on the other.

places.name: Matka Canyon
places.blurb: A steep-sided gorge and lake just outside Skopje, for kayaking, caves and cliffside monasteries.

BGR.summary: Old towns, mountain monasteries and a Black Sea coast.

places.name: Plovdiv
places.blurb: One of Europe's oldest cities: a Roman theatre still in use and a hillside old town of painted houses.

TUR.summary: Where Europe meets Asia: one vast historic city, then ruins, coast and strange landscapes inland.

places.name: Istanbul
places.blurb: Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque and the Grand Bazaar, in a city spread across two continents.

places.name: Cappadocia
places.blurb: Rock towers, cave churches and underground cities, best seen from a hot-air balloon at dawn.

GRC.summary: Ancient ruins on the mainland and hundreds of islands, each with its own character.

places.name: Athens
places.blurb: The Acropolis above a busy modern city, with some of the world's great ancient museums.

places.name: Crete
places.blurb: The largest Greek island: Minoan palaces, gorges and beaches. Big enough to need a car and most of a week.

places.name: Corfu
places.blurb: A green Ionian island with a Venetian old town and coves along the west coast.

places.name: Rhodes
places.blurb: A medieval walled city built by the Knights, with beaches and the acropolis of Lindos down the coast.

places.name: Mykonos
places.blurb: Whitewashed lanes, windmills and beach clubs, with the ruins of Delos a short boat ride away.

ROU.summary: A big, busy capital, then Transylvanian towns, castles and the Carpathian mountains.

places.name: Bucharest
places.blurb: Belle époque streets, a colossal parliament palace and a lively old town.

MDA.summary: A little-visited country of vineyards, wine cellars and Soviet-era streets.

places.name: Chisinau
places.blurb: A green, low-key capital, with vast underground wine cellars a short drive away.

places.name: Tiraspol
places.blurb: The capital of breakaway Transnistria, where Lenin statues and Soviet symbols are still in place.

UKR.summary: A large country of grand cities, wide steppe and a long history.

places.name: Chernobyl
places.blurb: The site of the 1986 nuclear disaster and the abandoned town of Pripyat. Closed to visitors since 2022.

BLR.summary: Wide boulevards, forests and a strong sense of the Soviet past.

places.name: Minsk
places.blurb: A capital rebuilt after the war in grand Soviet style, with broad avenues and big squares.

LTU.summary: A baroque capital, forests, lakes and a coast of sand dunes.

places.name: Vilnius
places.blurb: A large baroque old town of churches and courtyards, and the self-declared republic of Užupis.

LVA.summary: A handsome capital, pine forests and long sandy beaches.

places.name: Riga
places.blurb: A medieval old town, streets of art nouveau buildings and a market in old airship hangars.

EST.summary: A medieval capital, forests, bogs and islands.

places.name: Tallinn
places.blurb: A walled medieval old town of towers and merchants' houses, above a modern, digital-minded city.

FIN.summary: Design, saunas and lakes in the south, and the Arctic in the north.

places.name: Helsinki
places.blurb: A seaside capital of design shops, public saunas and a fortress on an island.

places.name: Lapland
places.blurb: The Arctic north: northern lights, reindeer and husky sleds in winter, the midnight sun in summer. Rovaniemi is the usual base.

SWE.summary: A capital built on islands, then forests, lakes and a long northern wilderness.

places.name: Stockholm
places.blurb: A city on fourteen islands: the old town of Gamla Stan, the Vasa ship and boats out to the archipelago.

ISL.summary: Volcanoes, glaciers, waterfalls and hot springs, around a small and lively capital.

places.name: Reykjavik
places.blurb: The world's northernmost capital: colourful houses, geothermal pools and day trips to geysers and waterfalls.

GEO.summary: Old churches, an ancient wine tradition and the high Caucasus, between the Black Sea and the mountains.

places.name: Tbilisi
places.blurb: Carved wooden balconies, sulphur baths and a fortress above the river, with food and wine to match.

places.name: Sighnaghi
places.blurb: A walled hilltop town above the vineyards of Kakheti, and the base for visiting wineries.

places.name: Gudauri
places.blurb: A ski resort high in the Greater Caucasus on the Georgian Military Highway, with hiking and paragliding in summer.

places.name: Batumi
places.blurb: A subtropical Black Sea resort with a long seafront boulevard and showy modern towers.

AZE.summary: An oil-rich capital on the Caspian Sea, with mud volcanoes and mountain villages beyond.

places.name: Baku
places.blurb: A walled old city beside flame-shaped skyscrapers, on a long Caspian seafront.

ARM.summary: Ancient monasteries in the mountains, around a pink-stone capital.

places.name: Yerevan
places.blurb: Pink stone buildings, pavement cafes and views of Mount Ararat, with old monasteries a short drive away.

ISR.summary: Holy sites, desert and a Mediterranean coast, in a small country.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.blurb: The walled Old City, holy to three faiths: the Western Wall, the Dome of the Rock and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.

XWB.summary: Hill towns and holy sites between Jerusalem and the Jordan valley.

places.name: Bethlehem
places.blurb: The Church of the Nativity on Manger Square, a short trip from Jerusalem.

CYP.summary: A sunny island of beaches, ancient ruins and mountain villages.

places.name: Paphos
places.blurb: A harbour town with Roman mosaics and rock-cut tombs, and beaches along the coast either side.

MLT.summary: Fortress cities, ancient temples and clear water, on small islands in the middle of the Mediterranean.

places.name: Valletta
places.blurb: A tiny fortified capital built by the Knights of St John, on a ridge between two harbours.

places.name: Gozo
places.blurb: Malta's quieter sister island, a short ferry ride away, with a hilltop citadel, temples and good diving.

QAT.summary: A desert peninsula with a fast-growing capital on the Gulf.

places.name: Doha
places.blurb: A waterfront skyline, the Museum of Islamic Art and the lanes of Souq Waqif.

ARE.summary: Futuristic cities on the Gulf, with desert and mountains behind.

places.name: Dubai
places.blurb: The world's tallest building, enormous malls and beaches, with the old creek and souks for contrast.

OMN.summary: Forts, wadis, desert and mountains, in the calmest corner of Arabia.

places.name: Muscat
places.blurb: A low white capital strung along the coast between rocky hills, with a grand mosque and an old souk.

RUS.summary: The largest country on Earth. Most visits centre on its two great cities.

places.name: Moscow
places.blurb: The Kremlin, Red Square and St Basil's, and a metro with stations like palaces.

places.name: Saint Petersburg
places.blurb: The tsars' capital: canals, palaces and the Hermitage, with white nights in June.

TKM.summary: One of the least-visited countries in the world: a marble capital and a burning crater in the desert.

places.name: Ashgabat
places.blurb: A capital of white marble, gold statues and wide, empty avenues.

places.name: Gates of Hell
places.blurb: The Darvaza gas crater, burning in the Karakum Desert since the 1970s. Camp nearby to see it after dark.

UZB.summary: The great Silk Road cities, with tiled mosques, madrasas and bazaars.

places.name: Samarkand
places.blurb: The Registan's three tiled madrasas, and the tombs and mosques of Tamerlane's capital.

places.name: Bukhara
places.blurb: A whole old town of mosques, madrasas and trading domes, still lived in.

places.name: Khiva
places.blurb: A walled desert city kept like an open-air museum, best at sunset from the walls.

places.name: Tashkent
places.blurb: The capital: Soviet-era metro stations, a big bazaar and the start of the fast train to Samarkand.

TJK.summary: A country that is almost all mountains, crossed by one of the world's great road journeys.

places.name: Pamir Highway
places.blurb: A high, rough road through the Pamir mountains between Dushanbe and Osh, taking about a week by 4x4.

places.name: Dushanbe
places.blurb: A leafy capital of wide avenues and teahouses, and where a Pamir trip begins.

KGZ.summary: High pastures, yurts and alpine lakes in the Tien Shan mountains.

places.name: Issyk Kul
places.blurb: A huge mountain lake that never freezes, with beaches on the north shore and snowy peaks all round.

places.name: Song-Kul
places.blurb: A high lake among summer pastures, where you stay in a yurt with herding families. Reachable June to September.

places.name: Karakol
places.blurb: A small town at the eastern end of Issyk Kul, and the base for trekking in the Tien Shan.

places.name: Bishkek
places.blurb: A green, Soviet-planned capital with mountains on the horizon and a big bazaar.

KAZ.summary: A vast country of steppe, with mountains along its southern edge.

places.name: Almaty
places.blurb: A leafy city at the foot of the Tien Shan, with ski slopes, canyons and lakes close by.

NPL.summary: The highest mountains on Earth, with temple cities and lakeside towns in the valleys below.

places.name: Kathmandu
places.blurb: Temple squares, stupas and crowded bazaars, and where almost every trip to Nepal begins.

places.name: Pokhara
places.blurb: A relaxed lakeside town under the Annapurna range, and the start of its treks.

places.name: Everest Base Camp
places.blurb: The classic trek through Sherpa villages to the foot of the world's highest mountain. About twelve days from the airstrip at Lukla.

places.name: Annapurna Base Camp
places.blurb: A trek from near Pokhara up through rhododendron forest into a ring of peaks. About a week to ten days.

PRK.summary: The most closed country in the world, seen only on a guided tour.

places.name: Pyongyang
places.blurb: A showpiece capital of monuments, wide avenues and vast squares. Visits are only possible on an organised, escorted tour.

KOR.summary: A high-energy capital, mountain temples and some of Asia's best food.

places.name: Seoul
places.blurb: Royal palaces among skyscrapers, night markets and neighbourhoods that stay up late.

TWN.summary: A mountainous island of night markets, hot springs and marble gorges.

places.name: Taipei
places.blurb: Night markets, the Taipei 101 tower and one of the world's great museums of Chinese art.

places.name: Hualien
places.blurb: A small east-coast city between the mountains and the Pacific, and the gateway to Taroko Gorge.

places.name: Kaohsiung
places.blurb: A warm southern port city with a redeveloped harbour, temples on a lotus lake and good seafood.

places.name: Taichung
places.blurb: A relaxed city of museums and cafes, where bubble tea began, and the way to Sun Moon Lake.

HKG.summary: A dense, vertical city of harbour views, markets and food, with green hills behind.

places.name: Kowloon
places.blurb: The mainland side of the harbour: the skyline view from Tsim Sha Tsui, night markets and crowded neon streets.

KHM.summary: The temples of Angkor, a riverside capital, and quiet towns and islands in the south.

places.name: Siem Reap
places.blurb: The town beside the temples of Angkor. Three days covers Angkor Wat, the Bayon and the jungle-covered Ta Prohm.

places.name: Phnom Penh
places.blurb: A riverside capital with the Royal Palace, busy markets and the sobering memorials of the Khmer Rouge years.

places.name: Koh Rong
places.blurb: An island of white-sand beaches and jungle, a ferry ride from Sihanoukville.

places.name: Kampot
places.blurb: A sleepy river town of old shophouses, known for its pepper farms and the hill station of Bokor.

places.name: Battambang
places.blurb: A quiet city of colonial streets, with countryside temples and the bamboo train nearby.

LAO.summary: Temples, karst mountains and slow travel along the Mekong.

places.name: Luang Prabang
places.blurb: A former royal capital of gilded temples and French-era streets on the Mekong, with the Kuang Si waterfalls nearby.

places.name: Vang Vieng
places.blurb: A riverside town among limestone cliffs, for caves, blue lagoons, kayaking and hot-air balloons.

places.name: Nong Khiaw
places.blurb: A quiet village on the Nam Ou river, hemmed in by huge karst mountains, with viewpoint hikes and boat trips.

places.name: Vientiane
places.blurb: One of the world's sleepiest capitals, with golden stupas and sunset on the Mekong.

places.name: Houayxay
places.blurb: The border town opposite Thailand where the two-day slow boat down the Mekong begins.

places.name: Pak Beng
places.blurb: A small riverside village, and the overnight stop on the slow boat to Luang Prabang.

THA.summary: Temples and mountains in the north, a huge capital in the middle, and islands and beaches down both coasts.

places.name: Bangkok
places.blurb: The Grand Palace, riverside temples, markets and street food, in a city that never slows down.

places.name: Chiang Mai
places.blurb: A walled old city full of temples, with night markets, cooking classes and mountains all round.

places.name: Koh Phi Phi
places.blurb: Sheer limestone cliffs around turquoise bays, with boat trips to Maya Bay.

places.name: Krabi
places.blurb: Limestone cliffs straight out of the sea, with Railay Beach and island-hopping by longtail boat.

places.name: Phuket
places.blurb: Thailand's biggest island. Kata Beach, in the south-west, is one of the more relaxed places to stay.

places.name: Koh Samui
places.blurb: A large Gulf island with palm-fringed beaches, from busy Chaweng to quieter coves.

places.name: Koh Tao
places.blurb: A small island and one of the cheapest and most popular places in the world to learn to dive.

places.name: Koh Lanta
places.blurb: A long, laid-back island of quiet beaches and sunsets, with an old fishing town on the east side.

places.name: Khao Sok
places.blurb: Ancient rainforest and a lake of limestone towers, where you can sleep in a floating bungalow.

places.name: Pai
places.blurb: A backpacker town in a mountain valley, reached by a road of several hundred bends from Chiang Mai.

places.name: Chiang Rai
places.blurb: The far north, known for the dazzling White Temple and the Blue Temple.

places.name: Koh Yao Noi
places.blurb: A quiet island in Phang Nga Bay, with rice fields, fishing villages and views of the karst islands.

places.name: Koh Yao Yai
places.blurb: The larger and even sleepier of the Yao islands, between Phuket and Krabi.

places.name: Pattaya
places.blurb: A big, brash beach resort two hours from Bangkok, with islands just offshore.

places.name: Surat Thani
places.blurb: The mainland transport hub for the Gulf islands and Khao Sok.

places.name: Hat Yai
places.blurb: The big city of the deep south, known for its markets and food, and the usual stop before Malaysia.

places.name: Chiang Khong
places.blurb: A small Mekong town at the border bridge to Laos, where travellers cross to the slow boat.

SGP.summary: A small, green and very orderly city-state, with some of the best food in Asia.

places.name: Singapore
places.blurb: Gardens by the Bay, Marina Bay's skyline, hawker centres and the old streets of Chinatown and Little India.

PHL.summary: More than seven thousand islands, with some of the clearest water and best beaches in Asia.

places.name: Palawan
places.blurb: A long, wild island of limestone cliffs and hidden lagoons, with El Nido as the base for island-hopping.

places.name: Coron
places.blurb: Jagged islands, clear lakes and some of the best wreck diving in the world, north of Palawan.

places.name: Boracay
places.blurb: A small island famous for the four kilometres of powdery sand at White Beach.

places.name: Cebu
places.blurb: The hub of the central islands: an old Spanish city, with waterfalls, canyoning and diving around the island.

IDN.summary: A chain of thousands of islands, from temples and volcanoes on Java to dragons and reefs in the east.

places.name: Yogyakarta
places.blurb: Java's cultural capital, and the base for the great temples of Borobudur and Prambanan.

places.name: Komodo Island
places.blurb: The home of the Komodo dragon, with pink beaches and superb diving. Boats go from Labuan Bajo on Flores.

places.name: Jakarta
places.blurb: The vast, crowded capital on Java, where most international flights arrive.

AUS.summary: A continent of its own: beach cities, reef and rainforest on the coasts, and the red desert in the middle.

places.name: Sydney
places.blurb: The Opera House and Harbour Bridge, ferries across the harbour and surf beaches from Bondi to Manly.

places.name: Great Barrier Reef
places.blurb: The world's largest coral reef, for snorkelling, diving and sailing. Boats go from the Whitsundays, Cairns and Port Douglas.

places.name: Uluru
places.blurb: The great red rock at the centre of the continent, sacred to the Anangu, best at sunrise and sunset.

places.name: Melbourne
places.blurb: Laneway cafes and bars, street art, big sporting events and the country's best food scene.

places.name: Great Ocean Road
places.blurb: A coastal drive west of Melbourne past surf beaches and rainforest to the sea stacks of the Twelve Apostles.

places.name: K'gari
places.blurb: The world's largest sand island, formerly Fraser Island: freshwater lakes, rainforest and a beach you drive along by 4x4.

places.name: Cairns
places.blurb: A tropical city in the far north, between the reef and the Daintree Rainforest.

places.name: Brisbane
places.blurb: A sunny river city with a man-made beach on the South Bank and islands in the bay.

places.name: Byron Bay
places.blurb: A laid-back surf town at Australia's most easterly point, with a lighthouse walk and whales offshore in winter.

places.name: Blue Mountains
places.blurb: Sandstone cliffs, eucalyptus valleys and the Three Sisters, two hours by train from Sydney.

places.name: Hobart
places.blurb: Tasmania's harbour capital, with the Salamanca market, the MONA art museum and a mountain looming behind.

places.name: Cradle Mountain
places.blurb: A jagged peak above a glacial lake in the Tasmanian wilderness, with wombats on the walking tracks.

places.name: Bay of Fires
places.blurb: White beaches and orange-lichened granite boulders on Tasmania's north-east coast.

places.name: Kangaroo Island
places.blurb: Sea lions, koalas and kangaroos in the wild, and a rugged coast, a ferry ride from the mainland near Adelaide.

places.name: Perth
places.blurb: A sunny, isolated city on the Indian Ocean, with Fremantle's port and the quokkas of Rottnest Island.

places.name: Magnetic Island
places.blurb: A hilly island of bays and boulders off Townsville, with wild koalas along the walking tracks.

places.name: Darwin
places.blurb: The tropical capital of the Top End, and the way in to Kakadu and Litchfield national parks.

places.name: Adelaide
places.blurb: A relaxed, easy city with a great food market, beaches and the Barossa wine region an hour away.

places.name: Gold Coast
places.blurb: A long strip of surf beaches backed by high-rises, with theme parks and rainforest inland.

places.name: Alice Springs
places.blurb: The outback town in the Red Centre, among the gorges of the MacDonnell Ranges.

places.name: Rainbow Beach
places.blurb: A small beach town under cliffs of coloured sand, and a jumping-off point for K'gari.

places.name: Townsville
places.blurb: A dry-tropics city with a seafront promenade and the ferry to Magnetic Island.

places.name: Mornington Peninsula
places.blurb: Bay beaches, wineries and hot springs, an hour south of Melbourne.

places.name: Coffs Harbour
places.blurb: A beach city halfway between Sydney and Brisbane, with a harbour walk and the Big Banana.

places.name: Woolgoolga
places.blurb: A small surf town north of Coffs Harbour, with a headland for whale watching and a large Sikh temple.

places.name: Canberra
places.blurb: The planned capital, with the national museums, galleries and Parliament House.

FJI.summary: More than three hundred islands in the South Pacific, with warm water, coral reefs and a famously friendly welcome.

places.name: Yasawa Islands
places.blurb: A chain of volcanic islands with empty beaches and blue lagoons, reached by a daily catamaran from Port Denarau.

places.name: Nadi
places.blurb: Where international flights arrive, and the jumping-off point for the islands from nearby Port Denarau.

places.name: South Sea Island
places.blurb: A tiny coral island in the Mamanucas you can walk round in minutes, half an hour by boat from Port Denarau.

places.name: Suva
places.blurb: The capital, on the wetter side of the main island, with a big produce market, colonial buildings and the Fiji Museum.

TUV.summary: One of the smallest and least-visited countries in the world: a few low coral atolls in the middle of the Pacific.

places.name: Funafuti
places.blurb: The main atoll and capital, a thin strip of land around a huge lagoon, where the airstrip doubles as the village green.

places.name: Funafala
places.blurb: A quiet islet at the southern end of Funafuti's lagoon, with a handful of families and a beach, reached by boat.

KEN.summary: The classic safari country: open savannah, big cats and the great wildebeest migration.

places.name: Masai Mara
places.blurb: Rolling grassland full of lions, cheetahs and elephants, with the wildebeest migration crossing from July to October.

places.name: Nairobi
places.blurb: A big, busy capital with a national park on its edge, an elephant orphanage and a giraffe centre.

EGY.summary: Five thousand years of history along the Nile, from the pyramids to the temples of the south.

places.name: Pyramids of Giza
places.blurb: The Great Pyramid and the Sphinx on the desert edge of Cairo, with the Grand Egyptian Museum close by.

places.name: Cairo
places.blurb: A vast, noisy, absorbing city on the Nile, with medieval mosques, bazaars and Coptic churches.

UGA.summary: Green hills, great lakes and forests that are home to mountain gorillas and chimpanzees.

places.name: Bwindi Gorilla Trek
places.blurb: A hike into Bwindi Impenetrable Forest for an hour with a family of wild mountain gorillas. Permits are limited, so book months ahead.

places.name: Kampala
places.blurb: A lively capital spread over hills near Lake Victoria, with markets, music and the old Buganda royal sites.

TZA.summary: Africa's highest mountain, its most famous plains and a spice island in the Indian Ocean.

places.name: Serengeti
places.blurb: Endless plains and the greatest concentration of big animals in Africa, with the migration moving through all year.

places.name: Ngorongoro Crater
places.blurb: A collapsed volcano whose floor is packed with wildlife, including black rhino, seen on a day's drive from the rim.

places.name: Zanzibar
places.blurb: The alleys and carved doors of Stone Town, spice farms, and white-sand beaches for the end of a safari.

places.name: Kilimanjaro
places.blurb: The highest mountain in Africa, climbed without ropes in six to eight days. Treks start from Moshi.

places.name: Iringa
places.blurb: A cool highland town on the road south, and the way in to Ruaha National Park.

MWI.summary: A small, friendly country strung along a huge freshwater lake.

places.name: Kande Beach
places.blurb: A sandy bay on Lake Malawi, for swimming, snorkelling among bright cichlid fish and village visits.

places.name: Chitipa
places.blurb: A small town in the far north, near the borders with Tanzania and Zambia, and a stop for overland travellers.

ZMB.summary: Wild, uncrowded national parks and the birthplace of the walking safari.

places.name: South Luangwa National Park
places.blurb: One of Africa's great parks, known for leopards, huge hippo pools and safaris on foot. Mfuwe is the base.

places.name: Lusaka
places.blurb: The capital and transport hub, with busy markets and the main airport.

places.name: Chipata
places.blurb: A border town near Malawi, and the last stop for supplies on the way to South Luangwa.

ZWE.summary: One of the world's great waterfalls, with national parks and ancient ruins beyond.

places.name: Victoria Falls
places.blurb: The Zambezi dropping more than a hundred metres along a mile-wide edge, with rafting, bungee jumps and sunset cruises.

BWA.summary: Some of the best wildlife in Africa, in a country that keeps its wilderness uncrowded.

places.name: Okavango Delta
places.blurb: A river that spreads into the Kalahari and never reaches the sea, explored by dugout canoe. Trips start from Maun.

places.name: Chobe National Park
places.blurb: The largest elephant herds in Africa, best seen from a boat on the Chobe River. Kasane is the base.

ZAF.summary: Big game, wine country and dramatic coast, at the southern tip of the continent.

places.name: Cape Town
places.blurb: Table Mountain above the sea, penguins at Boulders Beach, the Cape of Good Hope and vineyards an hour away.

places.name: Kruger National Park
places.blurb: A park the size of a small country, where you can drive yourself in search of the Big Five.

places.name: Johannesburg
places.blurb: The country's biggest city, with the Apartheid Museum, Soweto and the main international airport.

MAR.summary: Walled medinas, the Atlas mountains and the edge of the Sahara, a short flight from Europe.

places.name: Marrakesh
places.blurb: The red city: the great square of Jemaa el-Fna, souks, palaces and gardens, with the Atlas mountains on the horizon.

places.name: Fez
places.blurb: The largest medieval old city in the world still lived in, a maze of nine thousand lanes, tanneries and craft workshops.

places.name: Merzouga
places.blurb: A village at the foot of the Erg Chebbi dunes, for a camel ride into the Sahara and a night in a desert camp.

places.name: Tangier
places.blurb: A white port city facing Spain across the strait, with a hilltop kasbah and a long literary past.

places.name: Agadir
places.blurb: A modern Atlantic resort with a long sandy beach, and surf villages just up the coast.

BRA.summary: A country the size of a continent: beach cities, rainforest and some of the world's biggest waterfalls.

places.name: Rio de Janeiro
places.blurb: Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and the beaches of Copacabana and Ipanema, in a city squeezed between mountains and sea.

places.name: Iguazu Falls
places.blurb: Hundreds of waterfalls in the rainforest on the border with Argentina. See both sides: Brazil for the view, Argentina for the walkways.

COL.summary: Colonial towns, coffee hills and a Caribbean coast, in a country that has opened up to visitors.

places.name: Cartagena
places.blurb: A walled colonial city on the Caribbean, with bright balconied streets and islands offshore.

places.name: Medellin
places.blurb: The city of eternal spring, in a green valley, known for its cable cars, street art and nightlife.

places.name: Bogota
places.blurb: A high-altitude capital with the Gold Museum, the old quarter of La Candelaria and a cable car up Monserrate.

places.name: Guatape
places.blurb: A lakeside town of brightly painted houses, beside a giant rock with 700 steps to the top. A day trip from Medellin.

ECU.summary: Andean cities, cloud forest and the wildlife of the Galapagos, in one small country.

places.name: Galapagos
places.blurb: Volcanic islands far out in the Pacific, where giant tortoises, sea lions and iguanas have no fear of people. Seen by cruise or island-hopping.

places.name: Quito
places.blurb: A capital high in the Andes with a large colonial old town, almost on the equator.

PER.summary: Inca ruins in the Andes, the Amazon rainforest and one of the world's great cuisines.

places.name: Cusco
places.blurb: The old Inca capital, high in the Andes, and the base for the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu. Give yourself time to adjust to the altitude.

places.name: Inca Trail
places.blurb: The classic four-day trek over mountain passes to arrive at Machu Picchu at dawn. Permits sell out months ahead.

places.name: Salkantay Trek
places.blurb: A five-day alternative route to Machu Picchu, over a high pass beneath a glaciated peak, with no permit needed.

places.name: Peruvian Amazon
places.blurb: Rainforest lodges up the river from Puerto Maldonado, with macaws, monkeys, caimans and giant otters.

places.name: Arequipa
places.blurb: A city of white volcanic stone beneath three volcanoes, and the way to the condors of Colca Canyon.

places.name: Lima
places.blurb: The capital on the Pacific cliffs, where most trips begin, known above all for its food.

BOL.summary: High plains, salt flats and Andean cities, in one of South America's most striking landscapes.

places.name: Uyuni Salt Flats
places.blurb: The world's largest salt flat, a blinding white plain that turns into a mirror after rain. Usually seen on a three-day 4x4 tour.

CHL.summary: A long, thin country running from desert in the north to glaciers in the south.

places.name: Torres del Paine W Trek
places.blurb: A four or five day hike in Patagonia past granite towers, a hanging glacier and turquoise lakes.

places.name: Santiago
places.blurb: The capital, beneath the Andes, with good food and wine and the port of Valparaiso close by.

ARG.summary: Tango and steak in the capital, then glaciers and mountains at the bottom of the world.

places.name: Buenos Aires
places.blurb: Grand avenues, tango, late dinners and distinct neighbourhoods, from colourful La Boca to leafy Palermo.

places.name: Patagonia
places.blurb: The Perito Moreno glacier near El Calafate, and the hiking trails under Mount Fitz Roy at El Chalten.

places.name: Ushuaia
places.blurb: The southernmost city in the world, on the Beagle Channel, and where most ships to Antarctica leave from.

URY.summary: A small, relaxed country of beaches, old towns and open ranchland.

places.name: Montevideo
places.blurb: An easy-going capital with a long waterfront promenade, an old town and steak grilled in the port market.

places.name: Punta del Este
places.blurb: South America's smartest beach resort, on a peninsula between a calm bay and Atlantic surf.

PAN.summary: The narrow link between two continents and two oceans, with rainforest on both sides of the canal.

places.name: Panama Canal
places.blurb: Watch ocean-going ships rise through the Miraflores Locks, on the edge of Panama City.

GTM.summary: Maya ruins in the jungle, colonial streets, and a highland lake ringed by volcanoes.

places.name: Antigua
places.blurb: A colonial town of cobbled streets and ruined churches, overlooked by three volcanoes.

places.name: Lake Atitlan
places.blurb: A deep highland lake beneath three volcanoes, with Maya villages around the shore linked by boat.

places.name: Tikal
places.blurb: Maya temples rising above the rainforest canopy, with howler monkeys in the trees. Be there for sunrise.

places.name: Acatenango Hike
places.blurb: A steep overnight climb from Antigua to camp near the summit and watch the neighbouring Fuego volcano erupt after dark.

places.name: Flores
places.blurb: A small, colourful town on an island in a lake, and the base for visiting Tikal.

places.name: Xela
places.blurb: Quetzaltenango, known to everyone as Xela: a highland city popular for Spanish schools, volcano hikes and hot springs.

BLZ.summary: A small English-speaking country on the Caribbean, with a long barrier reef and jungle inland.

places.name: Caye Caulker
places.blurb: A small, sandy island with no cars and a go-slow motto, for snorkelling on the barrier reef with rays and nurse sharks.

MEX.summary: Ancient cities, colonial towns, beaches on two oceans and one of the world's great cuisines.

places.name: Mexico City
places.blurb: A huge high-altitude capital with Aztec ruins, great museums, markets and street food, and the pyramids of Teotihuacan nearby.

places.name: Oaxaca
places.blurb: A colonial city known for its food, mezcal and crafts, below the hilltop ruins of Monte Alban.

places.name: Chichen Itza
places.blurb: The great Maya city of the Yucatan, with its stepped pyramid. Arrive at opening time to beat the heat and the coaches.

places.name: Cancun
places.blurb: A big Caribbean beach resort, and the main airport for the Yucatan and the Riviera Maya.

places.name: Juarez
places.blurb: Ciudad Juarez, a large border city on the Rio Grande, directly across the bridge from El Paso.

CAN.summary: Enormous and mostly wild: mountains and lakes in the west, big cities in the east, and the Arctic to the north.

places.name: Banff National Park
places.blurb: Turquoise lakes, glaciers and peaks in the Rockies, with a lively small town at the centre.

places.name: Lake Louise
places.blurb: A glacier-fed lake of milky blue under a wall of mountains, with Moraine Lake just up the road.

places.name: Vancouver
places.blurb: A city between ocean and mountains, with Stanley Park, good food and ski slopes in sight of downtown.

places.name: Niagara Falls
places.blurb: Three huge waterfalls on the border with the United States, best seen from the Canadian side and from the boat at their foot.

places.name: Toronto
places.blurb: Canada's biggest city, on Lake Ontario, with the CN Tower and some of the most varied neighbourhoods and food anywhere.

places.name: Churchill
places.blurb: A remote town on Hudson Bay, reached only by train or plane, for polar bears in autumn and beluga whales in summer.
